result.topic_en: Euler gives a numerical example of an experiment with a wide vessel and a horizontal tube to determine the friction coefficient alpha from the water height at which outflow begins.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 369

82. Huiusmodi ergo experimenta institui poterunt tubis non adeo angustis, vti modo ante exposito, vnde hic modus anteferri videtur. Cum enim tubi arctissimi, qui capillares vocari solent, singularibus proprietatibus sint praediti, semper dubium relinqueretur, vtrum, ob has proprietates, effluxus aquae per huiusmodi tubos non peculiarem patiatur perturbationem, qua valor ipsius $\alpha$ inde collectus incertus redderetur.

83. Vt exemplum huiusmodi experimentorum exhibeam, ponamus esse vas AAB amplissimum, tubi vero horizontalis BC longitudinem esse $b = 2$ pedum, et amplitudinem $gg = \frac{1}{625}$ pedis quadrati, ideoque $g = \frac{1}{25}$ ped. lumen autem eius $kk$ tam esse exiguum, vt $\mathfrak{g} = \frac{k^4}{g^4}$ pro nihilo haberi possit. Hinc ob vas AAB amplissimum, negligi poterit fractio $\frac{\alpha a}{f}$, et habebitur $\mathfrak{B} = e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} = 1 - \frac{1}{80}$, sumto $\alpha = \frac{1}{4000}$. Atque obtinebitur $v = a - \frac{a-30}{80} = \frac{79a-30}{80}$. Vt igitur aqua hoc casu actu effluat, necesse est, vt sit $a > \frac{30}{79}$ pedis.

84. Si posuissemus $\alpha = \frac{1}{6000}$, prodiisset $\mathfrak{B} = 1 - \frac{1}{120}$, et $v = a - \frac{a-30}{120} = \frac{119a-30}{120}$, aqua ergo effluere inciperet statim atque aquae in vase AB altitudo $a$ superaret $\frac{30}{119}$ ped. Cum igitur posito $\alpha$ incognito sit $\mathfrak{B} = 1 - 50\alpha$, et $v = a(1-50\alpha) - 1500\alpha$, augeatur sensim altitudo aquae in vase AB, donec aqua per orificium CC effluere incipiat, et notetur tum altitudo $AB = a$ in pedibus, erit $\alpha = \frac{a}{50a+1500}$.

85. Si idem experimentum alio tubo horizontali instituatur, cuius tam longitudo $b$, quam amplitudo $gg$,
Tom. VI. Nou. Com. A a a sit

items.quote: Cum enim tubi arctissimi, qui capillares vocari solent, singularibus proprietatibus sint praediti, semper dubium relinqueretur, vtrum, ob has proprietates, effluxus aquae per huiusmodi tubos non peculiarem patiatur perturbationem, qua valor ipsius $\alpha$ inde collectus incertus redderetur.
items.english: For since the narrowest tubes, which are usually called capillary, are endowed with special properties, a doubt would always remain whether, owing to these properties, the outflow of water through such tubes suffers some peculiar disturbance, by which the value of alpha derived from it would be rendered uncertain.

items.quote: augeatur sensim altitudo aquae in vase AB, donec aqua per orificium CC effluere incipiat, et notetur tum altitudo $AB = a$ in pedibus, erit $\alpha = \frac{a}{50a+1500}$.
items.english: Let the height of water in vessel AB be gradually increased until water begins to flow out through the orifice CC, and note then the height AB = a in feet; then alpha = a/(50a+1500).
